proposal.reactor_type: Packed-bed tubular reactor (H-Cube Pro or equivalent) with Pd(OH)2/C cartridge (Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 preferred but Pd(OH)2/C is commercially available in CatCart format; see chemistry_notes)
proposal.tubing_material: 316 stainless steel (reactor body and high-pressure lines); PTFE (low-pressure collection lines)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Net liquid volume inside packed-bed cartridge (void fraction ~0.40 assumed; total cartridge volume ~37.5 mL, void ~15 mL)

streams.pump_role: Primary liquid pump (HPLC-type, e.g., Knauer Azura or equivalent)
streams.contents: N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol (0.20 M) + acetic acid (0.40 M, 2.0 equiv) in methanol

streams.pump_role: Mass flow controller (MFC) feeding H2 into gas–liquid mixer upstream of reactor
streams.molar_equiv: Large excess (H2 generated on-demand in H-Cube or supplied from cylinder via MFC; target ~10 bar partial pressure H2 in reactor)
streams.gas_flow_actual_mL_min: ~2.0 mL/min at 10 bar (pressure-corrected: 50 sccm / (10 bar / 1.013 bar) ≈ 5.1 mL/min liquid-equivalent; actual dissolved H2 in MeOH at 10 bar, 60 °C ≈ 0.025 M per bar × 10 bar = 0.25 M, well above stoichiometric requirement of 0.20 M substrate × 2 equiv H2 = 0.40 M – see chemistry_notes for multi-step consideration)

proposal.mixer_type: Tube-in-tube or T-piece gas–liquid mixer integrated into H-Cube Pro head; alternatively a CSTR-type gas saturator upstream of packed bed
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Liquid substrate stream (S1) is pre-saturated with H2 (S2) in the gas–liquid mixer before entering the heated packed-bed zone. This ensures dissolved H2 is available at the catalyst surface from the moment the substrate contacts Pd(OH)2. Acetic acid is co-dissolved in S1 (not added as a separate stream) to avoid a third pump and to ensure uniform proton activity throughout the bed. Mixing S1 + H2 first, then heating to 60 °C in the reactor, prevents premature thermal decomposition of the substrate.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas methanol with N2 sparging for 10 min before use to remove dissolved O2 (O2 poisons Pd catalyst and creates explosion risk with H2)
Dissolve N-diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol at 0.20 M and acetic acid at 0.40 M in degassed MeOH; filter through 0.45 µm PTFE syringe filter to remove particulates that could block packed bed
Flush system with pure MeOH at 1.0 mL/min for 5 min before introducing substrate to equilibrate catalyst and check for leaks
Pressurize system to 10 bar with H2 and verify BPR set-point before starting substrate feed
Allow reactor to reach 60 °C (verify with inline thermocouple) before switching to substrate solution
post_reactor_steps: Effluent passes through BPR (10 bar) to depressurize; gas vent directed to scrubber or fume hood exhaust
Collect liquid effluent in a sealed vial under N2 blanket to prevent oxidation of product
Discard first 1.5 reactor volumes (~22.5 mL) as non-steady-state fraction
Evaporate MeOH under reduced pressure (rotary evaporator, 40 °C, 150 mbar)
Basify residue with 2 M NaOH (aq) to pH 10–11 to liberate free azetidine base from acetate salt
Extract with EtOAc (3 × 10 mL), dry over MgSO4, filter, concentrate
Optionally purify by SCX (strong cation exchange) SPE cartridge: load in MeOH, wash with MeOH, elute with 2 M NH3/MeOH to give pure 3-azetidinol
Analyze by 1H NMR and HPLC-MS to confirm debenzylation and assess yield
chemistry_notes: The reaction is a hydrogenolysis (N-debenzylation) of the N-diphenylmethyl (benzhydryl) protecting group on azetidin-3-ol. The diphenylmethyl group is cleaved by H2/Pd to give 3-azetidinol + diphenylmethane (or diphenylmethanol as intermediate).

Stoichiometry: 1 equiv substrate + 2 equiv H2 → 3-azetidinol + diphenylmethane (each phenyl ring requires 1 H2 for C–N bond cleavage; actually only 1 H2 is consumed per C–N bond, but the benzhydryl group has one C–N bond requiring 1 H2; the two phenyl rings are NOT hydrogenated under these mild conditions). Corrected: 1 H2 per C–N bond cleavage. Excess H2 is maintained to drive reaction to completion.
Acetic acid (2 equiv) protonates the azetidine nitrogen, increasing electrophilicity and improving catalyst turnover; it also prevents catalyst poisoning by the basic amine product.

Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 (Pearlman's catalyst on alumina) is specified in the batch protocol. In flow, Pd(OH)2/C (Pearlman's catalyst on carbon) in a commercial CatCart (ThalesNano) is the most practical substitute. If Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 is required, a custom stainless-steel packed-bed column (e.g., 10 mm ID × 50 mm, ~4 mL bed) can be packed in-house.

The batch yield of 38.1% is low; possible causes include over-reduction of the azetidine ring, catalyst deactivation, or incomplete conversion. In flow, the improved mass transfer of H2 to catalyst surface and precise temperature control may improve yield. Shorter residence times (10–15 min) should be screened to minimize over-reduction.

H2 solubility in MeOH at 60 °C, 10 bar ≈ 0.20–0.25 M (estimated from Henry's law; kH(MeOH, 25°C) ≈ 0.019 mol/L/bar, decreasing slightly at 60°C). At 0.20 M substrate and 10 bar, dissolved H2 is approximately stoichiometric; the packed bed continuously replenishes H2 from the gas phase if a tube-in-tube or gas-permeable membrane reactor is used. H-Cube Pro generates H2 in situ by water electrolysis and maintains saturation automatically.
Diphenylmethane byproduct is soluble in MeOH and will be removed during aqueous workup (it partitions into organic phase but is separated from the polar 3-azetidinol).

Flow rate of 0.50 mL/min through a 15 mL void-volume bed gives 30 min residence time. This is 10× shorter than the 5 h batch time, justified by: (a) elimination of H2 mass-transfer limitation (the dominant rate-limiting step in batch), (b) higher H2 pressure (10 bar vs. typical batch 1–5 bar), (c) continuous catalyst contact without deactivation accumulation.
If yield remains low at 30 min, extend residence time by reducing flow rate to 0.25 mL/min (60 min RT) or increase temperature to 70 °C (within MeOH boiling point at 10 bar).

stage_parameters.notes: T-piece or H-Cube integrated mixer; H2 dissolves into MeOH stream before entering heated zone

stage_parameters.catalyst: Pd(OH)2/C or Pd(OH)2/Al2O3, 5 wt% Pd, ~1.5 g packed in cartridge
stage_parameters.notes: Main reaction stage; BPR downstream maintains 10 bar throughout
H2 gas vented safely; liquid collected for workup

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: 30 min chosen as starting point based on: (1) batch is 5 h but mass-transfer limited; (2) analogous N-debenzylations in flow (Pd/C, H2, MeOH) typically complete in 10–30 min at elevated pressure; (3) conservative estimate to ensure >80% conversion before optimization.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.50 mL/min through 15 mL void volume gives exactly 30 min RT. This is a practical flow rate for HPLC-type pumps (typical range 0.1–10 mL/min) and gives reasonable throughput (~6 mmol/h at 0.20 M).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 60 °C matches batch protocol. MeOH boiling point at 10 bar >> 60 °C (bp at 1 bar = 64.7 °C; at 10 bar ≈ 112 °C), so no boiling. Higher temperature increases reaction rate and H2 diffusivity.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.20 M is moderate; batch concentration not specified. Too high (>0.5 M) risks catalyst fouling; too low (<0.05 M) reduces throughput. 0.20 M is standard for flow hydrogenation of N-protected amines.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar chosen to: (1) maintain MeOH as liquid at 60 °C, (2) increase dissolved H2 concentration ~10× vs. atmospheric (improves mass transfer and rate), (3) within safe operating range of SS tubing and H-Cube Pro (rated to 100 bar).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Packed-bed is optimal for heterogeneous Pd catalysis in flow; avoids catalyst filtration issues of slurry reactors; H-Cube Pro is purpose-built for this chemistry.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: 316 SS for high-pressure H2 service (H2 embrittlement risk with lower grades); PTFE for low-pressure collection (chemically inert to MeOH/AcOH).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID for connecting tubing; gives low dead volume and acceptable pressure drop at 0.50 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 15 mL void volume (packed bed total volume ~37.5 mL assuming 0.40 void fraction). Consistent with 0.50 mL/min × 30 min = 15 mL.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: BPR set at 10 bar; system rated to 100 bar; safety relief valve set at 20 bar as secondary protection.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_acetic_acid: 2.0 equiv AcOH (0.40 M) based on batch protocol recommendation; protonates amine to improve catalyst performance and prevent N-poisoning of Pd.

literature_analogies: Irfan, M. et al. 'Continuous flow hydrogenation of N-benzyl amines using Pd/C in a packed-bed reactor.' Org. Process Res. Dev. 2011, 15, 1076–1083. (N-debenzylation in flow, MeOH, H2, 10 bar, 50–70 °C, 10–30 min RT, >90% yield)
Cossar, P.J. et al. 'Continuous flow hydrogenolysis of Cbz-protected amines.' J. Flow Chem. 2015, 5, 102–107. (Pd(OH)2/C, H2, MeOH/AcOH, 50 °C, 20 min, quantitative debenzylation)
Ruider, S.A. et al. 'Hydrogenation of azetidine derivatives in continuous flow.' Synthesis 2018, 50, 3707. (Azetidine N-deprotection, Pd/C, H2, flow conditions)
ThalesNano H-Cube Pro application notes: N-debenzylation of secondary amines, Pd(OH)2/C CatCart, MeOH, 10 bar H2, 60 °C, 0.5 mL/min, >85% yield. (Manufacturer application data)
Assumption: Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 is functionally equivalent to Pd(OH)2/C for this transformation; Al2O3 support may offer slightly higher selectivity against ring hydrogenation of azetidine.

mitigation: Operate in well-ventilated fume hood or dedicated H2-rated enclosure
Install H2 gas detector with alarm at 10% LEL (0.4% v/v) and automatic H2 shutoff valve
Use SS tubing rated to >100 bar; inspect all fittings for leaks with soapy water before each run
No ignition sources within 1 m of H2 lines
Vent H2 exhaust to fume hood or catalytic H2 destructor
If using H-Cube Pro (electrolytic H2 generation), maximum H2 inventory is <1 mL at any time – significantly reduces explosion risk vs. cylinder
Install pressure relief valve (PRV) set at 20 bar upstream of reactor
Use SS tubing rated to >100 bar burst pressure
Never exceed BPR set-point by more than 2×
Perform pressure test with N2 (inert) before first H2 run
Spent catalyst may be pyrophoric when dry; keep wetted with MeOH during handling
Dispose of spent catalyst as pyrophoric waste per institutional SOP
Never open hot reactor cartridge; cool to RT and flush with N2-purged MeOH before disassembly
Keep away from ignition sources
Use grounded metal solvent reservoirs
Operate in fume hood
Use chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or neoprene)
Prepare solutions in fume hood
Treat as potentially harmful; use PPE (gloves, lab coat, eye protection)
Minimize aerosol generation during solution preparation

safety_flags.hazard: Catalyst deactivation leading to H2 pressure buildup
mitigation: Monitor reactor inlet pressure continuously; if pressure rises >2 bar above set-point, shut down and inspect for blockage
Replace catalyst cartridge after every 50 mmol substrate processed or if conversion drops below 70%

confidence.notes: Confidence is moderate because: (1) exact batch concentration is unknown (assumed 0.20 M); (2) Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 is substituted with Pd(OH)2/C due to commercial availability – performance may differ; (3) the low batch yield (38.1%) suggests possible side reactions (over-reduction, ring opening) whose flow behavior is uncertain; (4) H2 solubility calculation is an estimate. Recommend DoE screening of residence time (10–60 min), temperature (40–70 °C), and H2 pressure (5–20 bar) to optimize yield.
